title: silene vulgaris subsp. alpina
intro: Silene vulgaris subsp. alpina, commonly known as Alpine Catchfly, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the carnation family. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its purported health benefits, which include reducing inflammation, improving respiratory issues, and supporting the immune system. The therapeutic actions of Alpine Catchfly are attributed to its ability to calm the nervous system, promote relaxation, and exhibit antimicrobial properties. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
